question: According to the Delaware CDL Manual, sending or receiving a text message takes a driver's eyes off the road for an average of how long?
choice_a: 4.6 seconds
choice_d: 1 second
explanation: The manual states that texting takes your eyes from the road for an average of 4.6 seconds, during which a vehicle at 55 mph would travel 371 feet, the length of a football field.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-22

question: According to the manual, which action makes a driver "not in compliance" even if the driver intends to use the hands-free function afterward?
choice_a: Unsafely reaching for a mobile phone
choice_d: Keeping the phone within close proximity
explanation: The manual states that drivers are not in compliance if they unsafely reach for a mobile phone, even if they intend to use the hands-free feature.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-23

question: How does the Delaware CDL Manual distinguish "road rage" from "aggressive driving"?
choice_a: Road rage involves the intent to do harm to others or physically assault a driver or their vehicle, while aggressive driving does not require intent to harm
choice_b: They are exactly the same thing under the manual's definitions
choice_c: Aggressive driving only applies to commercial vehicles
choice_d: Road rage is a legal charge while aggressive driving carries no penalties
explanation: The manual defines aggressive driving as operating selfishly or pushily without regard for others, while road rage is defined as operating a vehicle with intent to do harm or physically assault another driver or vehicle.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-23

question: What does the manual say you should do first and foremost when confronted by an aggressive driver?
choice_a: Make every attempt to get out of their way
choice_b: Speed up to hold your position in the lane
choice_c: Make eye contact to show confidence
choice_d: Flash your headlights at them repeatedly
explanation: The manual lists getting out of the aggressive driver's way as the first and foremost action, along with avoiding eye contact and ignoring gestures.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-24

question: If your driver license states that corrective lenses are required, what does the manual say about driving without them?
choice_a: It is illegal to move a vehicle without using corrective lenses
choice_b: It is allowed as long as it is only for short distances
choice_c: It is allowed as long as you drive under 30 mph
choice_d: It is allowed only during daytime hours
explanation: The manual states that if your license requires corrective lenses, it is illegal to move a vehicle without using them, even for short distances.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-24

question: Which of the following is listed in the manual as a warning sign of driver fatigue?
choice_a: Trouble remembering the last few miles driven
choice_d: Improved lane control
explanation: The manual lists trouble remembering the last few miles driven, along with difficulty focusing, yawning, and drifting from your lane, as warning signs of fatigue.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-25

question: According to the manual, getting how many hours of sleep or less triples your risk of a fall-asleep crash?
choice_a: 6 hours
choice_d: 10 hours
explanation: Under "Are You At Risk?" the manual states that being sleep-deprived or fatigued, defined as 6 hours of sleep or less, triples your risk.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-25

question: According to the manual, roughly how far ahead can you see with low-beam headlights at night?
choice_a: About 250 feet
choice_d: About 1,000 feet
explanation: The manual states that with low beams you can see ahead about 250 feet, and with high beams about 350-500 feet, and you must adjust your speed to keep your stopping distance within your sight distance.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-26

question: Per the manual, within what distance of an oncoming or followed vehicle should you dim your headlights at night?
choice_a: 500 feet
choice_d: 200 feet
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to dim their lights within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle and when following another vehicle within 500 feet.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-27

question: What does the manual say is the "best advice" for driving in fog?
choice_a: Don't drive in fog; pull off the road into a rest area or truck stop until visibility improves
choice_b: Drive with your high beams on for maximum visibility
choice_c: Drive as fast as safely possible to get through the fog quickly
choice_d: Follow closely behind another vehicle's taillights
explanation: The manual states, "The best advice for driving in fog is don't," recommending you pull off the road until visibility is better.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-27

question: According to the manual, what is the minimum tread depth required on front tires for winter driving?
choice_a: 4/32 inch
choice_d: 1/32 inch
explanation: The manual states you must have at least 4/32 inch tread depth in every major groove on front tires and at least 2/32 inch on other tires.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-27

question: According to the manual, what can happen to your brakes after driving through deep water or heavy rain?
choice_a: They can become weak, apply unevenly, or grab, potentially causing wheel lockup, pulling to one side, or jackknife
choice_b: They automatically dry themselves within seconds with no effect on performance
choice_c: Only the parking brake is affected
choice_d: There is no effect on braking from wet conditions
explanation: The manual explains that water in the brakes can cause weak braking, uneven application, grabbing, wheel lockups, pulling to one side, and jackknife if pulling a trailer.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-28

question: In very hot weather, how often does the manual recommend inspecting your tires while driving?
choice_a: Every two hours or every 100 miles
choice_d: Only at the start of the trip
explanation: The manual states to inspect the tires every two hours or every 100 miles when driving in very hot weather, since air pressure increases with temperature.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-28

question: If there is no white stop line painted on the pavement, how close must a vehicle required to stop be to the nearest rail of the nearest track?
choice_a: No closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet
choice_d: There is no specified distance
explanation: The manual states that vehicles required to stop at a cross-buck sign, absent a painted stop line, must stop no closer than 15 feet or more than 50 feet from the nearest rail of the nearest track.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-29

question: According to the manual, how long does it take a typical tractor-trailer unit to clear a single railroad track?
choice_a: At least 14 seconds
choice_d: At least 60 seconds
explanation: The manual states it takes a typical tractor-trailer unit at least 14 seconds to clear a single track and more than 15 seconds to clear a double track.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-30

question: Which of the following is listed as a factor in selecting a "safe" speed for a long, steep downgrade?
choice_a: Total weight of the vehicle and cargo
choice_d: The number of passengers on board
explanation: The manual lists total weight of the vehicle and cargo, length and steepness of the grade, road conditions, and weather as factors in choosing a safe downgrade speed.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-31

question: Using the manual's recommended braking technique on a downgrade, how much should your speed be reduced below your "safe" speed before releasing the brakes?
choice_a: About 5 mph
choice_d: About 15 mph
explanation: The manual instructs applying the brakes until speed is reduced to approximately five mph below your safe speed, then releasing the brakes, with each application lasting about three seconds.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-31

question: What do escape ramps typically use to stop a runaway vehicle, according to the manual?
choice_a: A long bed of loose, soft material
choice_d: An electronic braking system built into the road
explanation: The manual describes escape ramps as using a long bed of loose, soft material to slow a runaway vehicle, sometimes combined with an upgrade.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-32

question: According to the manual, why might steering be preferable to braking in certain emergencies?
choice_a: You can almost always turn to miss an obstacle more quickly than you can stop
choice_b: Steering always causes less vehicle damage than braking
choice_c: Braking is illegal to use in emergency situations
choice_d: Steering uses less fuel than braking
explanation: The manual states that when you don't have enough room to stop, you may have to steer away from what's ahead because you can almost always turn to miss an obstacle more quickly than you can stop.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-32

question: With the "stab braking" method described in the manual, what should you do when the wheels lock up?
choice_a: Release the brakes, then reapply them fully once the wheels start rolling again
choice_b: Continue pressing the brake pedal harder until the vehicle stops
choice_c: Pump the brakes rapidly in short, light bursts
choice_d: Shift into neutral immediately
explanation: The manual explains that with stab braking, you apply the brakes fully and release them when the wheels lock up, then reapply fully once the wheels start rolling again.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-33

question: If you experience a loss of hydraulic brake pressure, which action does the manual recommend?
choice_a: Downshift to a lower gear to help slow the vehicle
choice_b: Immediately turn off the engine while moving
choice_c: Accelerate to reach the nearest service station
choice_d: Shift into neutral and coast to a stop
explanation: The manual lists downshifting into a lower gear as one of the things you can do when the hydraulic brake system loses pressure and the pedal feels spongy or goes to the floor.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-33

question: What is the primary function of an Antilock Braking System (ABS), according to the manual?
choice_a: It keeps your wheels from locking up during hard brake applications
choice_b: It automatically increases the vehicle's overall stopping power
choice_c: It replaces the normal braking system entirely
choice_d: It reduces the vehicle's overall weight
explanation: The manual defines ABS as a computerized system that keeps your wheels from locking up during hard brake applications, adding to but not replacing your normal brakes.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-34

question: According to the manual, ABS is required on truck tractors with air brakes built on or after what date?
choice_a: March 1, 1997
choice_d: July 1, 1995
explanation: The manual states the Department of Transportation requires ABS on truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-34

question: Which statement about ABS is accurate according to the manual's safety reminders?
choice_a: ABS won't allow you to drive faster, follow more closely, or drive less carefully
choice_b: ABS guarantees a shorter stopping distance in every situation
choice_c: ABS eliminates the need for regular brake maintenance
choice_d: ABS prevents all types of skids, including those caused by over-acceleration
explanation: The manual's safety reminders state ABS won't allow faster driving, closer following, or less careful driving, and won't necessarily shorten stopping distance or prevent power/turning skids.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-35

question: According to the manual, which of the following is one of the four listed causes of a skid?
choice_a: Over-braking, causing the wheels to lock up
choice_d: A dirty windshield
explanation: The manual lists over-braking, over-steering, over-acceleration, and driving too fast as the four causes of a skid; under-inflated tires is not among them.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-35

question: What is the first step in correcting a drive-wheel braking skid, according to the manual?
choice_a: Stop braking to let the rear wheels roll again
choice_b: Apply the brakes harder to force traction
choice_c: Turn the steering wheel away from the direction of the skid only
choice_d: Accelerate to try to regain traction
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to stop braking first, which lets the rear wheels roll again and keeps them from sliding, then to counter-steer.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-36

question: What are the three basic steps to take at any accident scene, per the manual?
choice_a: Protect the area, notify authorities, and care for the injured
choice_b: Call your dispatcher, take photos, and exchange insurance information
choice_c: Move all vehicles immediately, determine fault, and leave the scene
choice_d: Protect the cargo, notify the shipper, and continue the route
explanation: The manual lists protecting the area, notifying authorities, and caring for the injured as the basic steps to take at any accident when you are not seriously hurt.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-37

question: If you need to fight a fire on your vehicle, what does the manual specifically warn you NOT to do when pulling off the road?
choice_a: Don't pull into a service station
choice_d: Don't stop the vehicle at all
explanation: The manual explicitly warns, "Don't pull into a service station!" when getting the vehicle off the road to fight a fire, and instead to park in an open area away from anything flammable.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-37

question: According to the manual, what is a B:C type fire extinguisher designed to work on?
choice_a: Electrical fires and burning liquids
choice_d: All fire types equally well
explanation: The manual states the B:C type fire extinguisher is designed to work on electrical fires and burning liquids, while the A:B:C type also works on burning wood, paper, and cloth.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-38

question: According to the manual, what is the only thing that will sober up a driver who has been drinking?
choice_a: Time
choice_d: Fresh air
explanation: The manual states that because the liver processes alcohol at a fixed rate, only time, not black coffee or a cold shower, will sober you up.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 2-39
